summary.text: Samsung Electronics announced preliminary Q3 2026 consolidated operating profit of KRW 107.4tn on revenue of KRW 195tn. Operating profit rose from KRW 89.5tn in the previous quarter and exceeded KRW 100tn for the first time; the figure is preliminary, before the close is finished.

This report's judgment is 'Add to Watchlist' with medium confidence. That is a research priority, not a buy or sell opinion or a judgment on position size, and no price-attractiveness analysis was done this time. The strongest counter-evidence is that profit leans heavily on memory prices and that the DS division produces virtually all operating profit.

Access to the DART body and notes was refused, so the consolidated statements and review report published by the company's IR were used instead; the segment note and the text of treasury-share filings could not be checked. This document is therefore a reviewed draft with research limits and is not a final report.
summary.qualification: Direct read of the DART body and notes failed

blocks.text: Samsung Electronics reports results by the DS division (semiconductors), the DX division (mobile, TV and appliances), its subsidiary Harman and Samsung Display (labelled 'Display' by the company). In Q2 2026, DS posted revenue of KRW 127.5tn and operating profit of KRW 89.2tn, generating virtually all of the consolidated operating profit of KRW 89.5tn, while DX recorded revenue of KRW 48tn with an operating loss of KRW 0.8tn.

blocks.title: Q2 2026 results by segment
blocks.basis: Company-reported segment figures; segment revenues are before intra-group eliminations and do not sum to consolidated revenue

blocks.text: Segment operating profits (89.2 − 0.8 + 0.4 + 0.7) add up to the consolidated KRW 89.5tn within rounding. Segment revenues, by contrast, add up to KRW 187.6tn, above the consolidated KRW 171.5tn, because intra-group transactions are eliminated on consolidation; summing segment revenue to compute shares would be misleading.

Within DX, the company said mobile (MX) revenue rose year on year on Galaxy S26 and A-series sales but profit fell on higher component costs, and appliances revenue rose quarter on quarter while profit fell on costs. The same memory-price increase is a profit for the chip division and a cost for the set businesses, and both sit inside one company.

Segment figures for Q3 have not been released. The preliminary announcement contains only consolidated revenue and operating profit, so all Q3 segment figures below are broker estimates and are labelled as such.
blocks.qualification: Q3 segment figures are not company-reported and are broker estimates

blocks.text: Across the latest eight filed quarters (2024-Q3 to 2026-Q2), revenue rose from KRW 79.1tn to KRW 171.5tn and operating profit from KRW 9.2tn to KRW 89.5tn. Operating profit has risen quarter on quarter every quarter since the KRW 4.7tn low in 2025-Q2, and including the preliminary Q3 figure (KRW 107.4tn) that is the fifth consecutive increase.

blocks.title: Quarterly operating and net margins
blocks.basis: Consolidated; net profit attributable to owners

blocks.title: Quarterly ledger and Q3 preliminary figures
blocks.basis: Consolidated. Q4 values are derived as full year minus nine-month cumulative; the Q3 preliminary figure is pre-close and has no net profit

blocks.text: Preliminary Q3 revenue of KRW 195tn is up 13.7% from the previous quarter and 126.6% from a year earlier, and operating profit is up 20.0% from the previous quarter. The company states a year-on-year operating-profit increase of 782.50%, whereas recomputing from the rounded KRW 107.4tn gives about 782.8%, which suggests the company calculated from unrounded values. Against the FnGuide consensus of KRW 108.7tn for Q3 operating profit, the preliminary figure is about 1.2% lower.
blocks.qualification: Consensus is the FnGuide aggregate as reported on 10/1; the rounding explanation is the author's inference

blocks.text: Gross margin rose from 34.2% in 2025-Q2 to 61.2% in 2026-Q1 and 69.6% in 2026-Q2. Over that period cost of sales grew only about 6%, from KRW 49.1tn to KRW 52.2tn, while revenue grew 2.3-fold, so nearly all of the profit increase can be read as coming from selling prices and product mix rather than cost cuts.

For Q3, brokers estimate that average DRAM selling prices rose 19–21% quarter on quarter while shipments grew 3–4%, and that HBM sales roughly doubled. These point to a price effect larger than a volume effect, but they are estimates and not figures confirmed by the company.
blocks.qualification: Broker estimates that may differ from the confirmed results

blocks.text: Net profit runs at about 80% of operating profit (82.3% in 2026-Q1 and 79.6% in Q2), and nothing unusual in the conversion from operating to net profit appeared in the range read. However, the notes breaking down financial income, equity-method gains and income taxes were not read, so the absence of one-off items is not asserted.

Whether the profit can repeat depends on the price cycle. Annual operating margin was 2.5% in 2023, 10.9% in 2024 and 13.1% in 2025, then reached 52.2% in 2026-Q2; margins in the same business have moved more than twenty-fold in three years, which shows how volatile they can be.

blocks.text: Operating cash flow was 70% of operating profit in 2026-Q1, 117% in Q2 and 99% for the first half, against 196% for full-year 2025. Because the business has heavy depreciation, cash flow normally exceeds operating profit, so the 99% in the first half hints that part of the profit growth may have been tied up in receivables, inventory or taxes. Trade receivables were KRW 96.4tn and inventories KRW 71.4tn at end-June, but their change from year-end was not checked, so no cause is asserted.

sections.title: Industry, competitors, growth thesis and counter-evidence

blocks.title: Three memory makers compared
blocks.basis: Samsung consolidated and DS division / SK hynix consolidated (secondary report) / Micron on its fiscal year (currency, period and business scope differ)
rows: Preliminary revenue KRW 195tn, operating profit KRW 107.4tn
Consensus operating profit KRW 77.2tn (not yet reported)
blocks.qualification: Periods, currencies and business scope differ, so this is not a like-for-like comparison; SK hynix and Micron figures come from secondary reports

blocks.text: The core of the growth thesis is that AI server demand keeps outrunning memory supply for a long stretch. Micron said demand will exceed supply in 2027–2028, and SK hynix said it has finished talks on long-term supply agreements, typically five years, with more than ten customers; both support the thesis.
blocks.qualification: Statements are management outlooks and were not independently verified

blocks.text: On the counter side, Morgan Stanley expects the year-on-year growth rate of DRAM contract prices to peak in 2026-Q4, and China's CXMT, which is still adding capacity (7.67% of DRAM revenue in 2025-Q4), is cited as a supply variable. One analysis also says Samsung may have greater short-term exposure than HBM-centred SK hynix because of its higher share of commodity and mobile DRAM sold to Chinese customers.
blocks.qualification: Broker and press analysis; the timing of the price peak is a forecast

blocks.text: In HBM, Samsung said it was first in the industry to ship HBM4 in volume in February and first to ship HBM4E samples in Q2. However, Nvidia supply and a 28–30% HBM4 share rest on reports and unnamed market-research estimates, and SK hynix also began HBM4 mass shipments in Q2, so the competition is ongoing.
blocks.qualification: Nvidia supply and share are company claims and unnamed estimates; customer confirmation not read

blocks.text: CXMT said at an event in Shanghai in October that it would show server DDR5 based on a 4F² cell structure within the year, but it disclosed no specifications, yield, mass-production schedule or customers. Samsung presented a 16Gb 4F² test chip at ISSCC in February and is reported to target sub-10nm DRAM mass production by 2028, so there is no evidence that Samsung is simply behind in this technology race.
blocks.qualification: CXMT's mass production and customer qualification are unconfirmed; Samsung's target date is as reported

lead.text: Add to Watchlist (research priority, medium confidence): this is a period in which the quality and durability of profit are well worth verifying directly.

grounds.text: Grounds: operating profit has risen for five straight quarters including the preliminary Q3 figure, after the 2025-Q2 low, and cash plus short-term financial instruments of KRW 190.0tn at end-June are far above borrowings of KRW 22.4tn.

conditions.text: What would change the view: slower Q4 DRAM price growth, mass production and customer qualification of CXMT's 4F² product, worse cash conversion of operating profit, and wider DX losses and compensation costs in the confirmed results.

sentences: Samsung Electronics' preliminary Q3 consolidated operating profit is KRW 107.4tn, against KRW 12.2tn in the same quarter of 2025, so the unit of profit has changed within a year.
Revenue of KRW 195tn is up 13.7% on the previous quarter and operating profit is up 20.0%, so profit grew faster than sales.
Whether this change is structural or temporary is the central question of this investigation, which is why the conclusion is presented as a research priority: 'Add to Watchlist'.
The preliminary announcement, however, contains no net profit, segment profit or cash flow, so the composition of profit can only be dissected with the confirmed data through Q2.
The strongest counter-argument is that this profit leans heavily on memory prices, an external variable, so the same leverage can work in reverse once the rate of price increases slows.
Investors should therefore look first not at the KRW 107.4tn headline but at how segment profit and gross margin are confirmed in the final results disclosure.
Operating margin rose from 8.4% in 2025-Q1 to 52.2% in 2026-Q2, and is 55.1% when computed from the preliminary Q3 figures.
The change shows most clearly in gross margin, which rose from 34.2% in 2025-Q2 to 61.2% in 2026-Q1 and 69.6% in Q2, while cost of sales grew only about 6% as revenue grew 2.3-fold.
Revenue growing with costs almost unchanged reads as selling prices and product mix, rather than volumes, driving profit, and the company's Q2 explanation also cited server demand and HBM expansion.
The mechanism is simple: chip manufacturing has a large fixed-cost share, so when prices rise most of the added revenue falls to profit, and when prices fall profit shrinks at the same speed.
That makes it risky to treat this high margin as a new baseline, and the fact that annual operating margin was 2.5% in 2023 shows how quickly the same business can move the other way.
The first observation point for the quality of profit is whether gross margin keeps rising from 69.6% in Q2 or stalls in the confirmed Q3 data.
Looking at Q2 segment results, the DS division recorded revenue of KRW 127.5tn and operating profit of KRW 89.2tn, producing virtually all of the consolidated KRW 89.5tn.
In the same quarter DX had an operating loss of KRW 0.8tn while Harman earned KRW 0.4tn and Display KRW 0.7tn, so the businesses outside semiconductors contributed only about KRW 0.3tn combined.

This asymmetry is estimated to have widened in Q3: one broker calculates that the mobile and networks loss grew from KRW 0.7tn to 1.8tn and the TV and appliances loss from about KRW 10bn to about KRW 400bn.

Because higher memory prices are profit for the chip division but a component cost for the set businesses, the same factor acts in opposite directions inside one company, and the scale is heavily lopsided.

The counter-argument is that this works as a natural hedge, easing the set businesses' burden when prices fall, but with DS profit tens to over a hundred times the DX loss it is hard to say the hedge stabilizes group profit.
The confirmed results, when segment figures are published, should therefore be used to check the durability of DS profit and the size of the DX loss separately.
paragraphs.qualification: Q3 segment figures are broker estimates and not company-confirmed

sentences: At June 30, 2026, cash and equivalents of KRW 92.9tn plus short-term financial instruments of KRW 97.0tn come to KRW 190.0tn, well above borrowings of KRW 22.4tn.
Net cash after subtracting borrowings is calculated at about KRW 167.5tn, a conservative figure that excludes long-term financial assets and similar items.
First-half operating cash flow was KRW 145.4tn and spending on tangible and intangible assets was KRW 33.0tn, leaving about KRW 112.4tn after funding capital expenditure.

By quarter, however, operating cash flow swung from 70% of operating profit in Q1 to 117% in Q2 and was 99% for the half; given 196% for full-year 2025, part of the profit growth may have been tied up in working capital.
Trade receivables were KRW 96.4tn and inventories KRW 71.4tn at end-June, but their change from year-end was not checked, so the cause is not asserted.
The conclusion that financial capacity is ample is supported by the numbers, but how fast profit turns into cash needs to be checked directly in the working-capital items of the Q3 report.
Views differ on how long this profit will last.

Morgan Stanley is reported to expect the year-on-year growth rate of DRAM contract prices to peak in the fourth quarter of 2026 and slow sharply in 2027, which does not mean prices fall at once but that the pace of increases slows.
Micron, by contrast, said in its September 30 results that demand will exceed supply in 2027 and 2028 and that more than 75% of fiscal 2027 shipments are already allocated to customers.
SK hynix also said it has finished talks on long-term supply agreements, typically five years, with more than ten customers, so demand-side signals are strong.

Yet share prices and earnings estimates tend to react to the rate of change rather than the level of prices, so the core of the peak thesis is that shares can wobble first, when growth in prices slows, even while demand is strong.
What decides this debate is therefore whether the Q4 contract-price growth rate and the price terms of long-term agreements become visible.
paragraphs.qualification: Reports views and statements of each institution; not independently verified

sentences: HBM is the gauge of whether Samsung is regaining share, and the company said in February that it was first in the industry to ship HBM4 in volume.
In its Q2 release it said it expanded HBM4 supply and was first in the industry to ship HBM4E samples, and broker estimates have Q3 HBM sales at about double Q2.
Nvidia supply and the 28–30% HBM4 share for 2026 depend on reports and market-research estimates with undisclosed sources, so they were not treated as established fact.
Competitor SK hynix began HBM4 mass shipments in Q2 and says talks on 2027 volumes and prices are going smoothly, showing that HBM4 is not a Samsung-only comeback story.
Micron also announced in February that it had begun HBM4 shipments, so the meaning of Samsung's 'first' claim depends on the timing gap between the company's announcement and its rivals'.
What investors should check is whether the final results call gives HBM revenue and customer mix in numbers, and whether they point the same way as broker estimates.
paragraphs.qualification: Nvidia supply and share are company claims and unnamed estimates; customer confirmation not read

sentences: China's CXMT said at an event in Shanghai in October that it would show server DDR5 using a 4F² cell structure within the year, and that news was one factor in the fall in Samsung and SK hynix shares from October 12.
4F² reduces cell area versus the existing 6F² structure, in theory fitting more cells into the same area, but CXMT disclosed no specifications, yield, mass-production schedule or customers.

CXMT held 7.67% of DRAM revenue in 2025-Q4, ranking fourth in the world, while Samsung, SK hynix and Micron still hold over 90%, so the threat lies in the pace of capacity expansion and technology catch-up rather than current share.
One analysis points out that Samsung may have greater short-term exposure than HBM-centred SK hynix because it has a higher share of Chinese customers in commodity and mobile DRAM.

On the other hand, Samsung presented a 16Gb 4F² test chip at ISSCC in February and is reported to target sub-10nm DRAM mass production by 2028, so it is not a one-sided victim of the technology catch-up.

Since there are also views that the market reaction has run ahead of confirmed supply, it is right not to assert the size of the threat until news of CXMT's mass-production results and customer qualification appears.
paragraphs.qualification: CXMT's mass production and customer qualification are unconfirmed; Samsung's target date is as reported

sentences: Shareholder returns sit under the 2024–2026 policy of returning 50% of three-year free cash flow, with the regular dividend at about KRW 9.8tn a year and quarterly per-share dividends of KRW 372 in Q1 and KRW 374 in Q2.

According to reports on the August 21 disclosure, the company estimated the remaining 2026 return pool at KRW 90–110tn, of which about KRW 30tn will be paid first as cash dividends including the regular Q3 dividend, with the rest and the method to be decided by the board at the end of January 2027.

A report said KRW 14.58tn of treasury shares would be cancelled on April 2, and the October 12 treasury-stock acquisition result report was filed on DART, but whether cancellation was completed and the details of the acquisition result were not checked because the filing text could not be read.
Resolution, execution, completed acquisition and completed cancellation have to be separated because the actual size of the return differs at each stage.
The counter-argument is that treasury-share purchases for employee bonuses are not counted as returns while reducing free cash flow, which cuts the pool available for a special dividend.
Brokers expect the new return policy to expand greatly, but this is an expectation ahead of the board's decision and should be kept distinct.
paragraphs.qualification: Return sizes are from reports and broker estimates ahead of the board decision; DART text not read

sentences: The wage and bonus package tentatively agreed on May 20 was reported as a structure that accrues 10.5% of DS division performance, with no cap, as a special bonus paid in shares over ten years.

Because the shares for employees must be bought in the market, estimates reported say that KRW 20–25tn of treasury-share purchases are needed this year and up to about KRW 90tn next year; these are broker estimates.
Those purchases are not counted as returns and reduce free cash flow, so by Mirae Asset's estimate remaining return capacity falls from KRW 117.5tn to KRW 103.9tn.
DX employees receive about KRW 6 million in shares and a different bonus cap, widening the pay gap between divisions, and reports said some DX union members pursued a no vote and an injunction.
Structurally, a fixed share of profit goes to employees, so in boom periods the shareholders' portion can grow more slowly than operating profit.

The same structure also lowers the risk of losing key staff and of strikes, so the cost cannot simply be called a loss, and the provisions for labour costs in the confirmed Q3 results should be checked.
paragraphs.qualification: Deal terms and purchase sizes are from reports and broker estimates; reports differ on 'business performance' versus 'operating profit'

sentences: What the memory boom is hiding is foundry and System LSI.
In its Q2 explanation, System LSI recorded its largest first-half revenue and Foundry improved on HBM base-die and U.S. customer demand, but no profit figures were disclosed.
An August report says Samsung has invested more than US$37bn in the Taylor, Texas fab, that filling Phase 1 utilization is the task, and that early 2nm yield has been hard to secure.
The rumored KRW 20tn Tesla AI5/AI6 order is an observation without a confirmed contract, so it was kept as something to watch and not as a growth thesis.
The report that TSMC holds most next-generation volume from Nvidia, Apple and AMD shows how uncertain it is how many outside customers Samsung can win.
Whether foundry turns profitable should be checked in the confirmed results with segment profit, and outside customer wins in official announcements.
paragraphs.qualification: Foundry status is a single outlet's report; profit and contracts unconfirmed

sentences: On October 13 Samsung's common shares closed down 7.39% at KRW 232,000, on the 15th they closed down 9.48% at KRW 210,000 as the KOSPI fell 7.57% and a circuit breaker was triggered.

On the 16th they rebounded 2.62% to close at KRW 215,500, after foreign investors net sold for eight straight sessions from October 2 to 15, with net selling of Samsung and SK hynix alone about KRW 16.4tn through the 15th and retail net buying of the two about KRW 7.1tn through the 14th.
Broker target prices as of October 7 ranged from KRW 270,000 to KRW 630,000, but they were issued before this sell-off, so comparing them directly with the current price would mislead.

Besides the CXMT news, a hotter-than-expected US September CPI, debt worries at AI cloud provider CoreWeave and foreign flows were cited as causes of the fall, so it is hard to attribute it to a deterioration in Samsung's own earnings.

A reported 52-week high of KRW 380,000 puts the current price KRW 215,500 about 43% lower, but that high comes from an auto-generated article whose figures do not match internally, so it is for reference only.

This report did not analyze price attractiveness, so it makes no judgment on whether the fall is an opportunity, and notes only that volatility of this size has to be weighed separately in any personal allocation decision.
paragraphs.qualification: Closing prices are from original press reports; the 52-week high is from a single auto-generated article

sentences: 'Add to Watchlist' means that the durability of profit, not its size, is worth verifying directly, and the priority will be raised or lowered if the conditions below are confirmed.

Conditions for raising the priority are that Q4 DRAM price growth holds up, that the confirmed results show HBM revenue and customer mix in numbers, and that operating cash flow recovers to the level of operating profit.

Conditions for lowering it are that DRAM average selling prices turn down, that CXMT's 4F² products move to mass production and major-customer qualification, or that DX losses and compensation costs eat into the profit growth.
Because the DART body and notes could not be read in this investigation, the judgment also needs to be revisited after checking the segment note and the commitments and contingencies notes.
The confirmed Q3 results, the Q3 report and the board's return decision announced for the end of January 2027 are the schedule that will supply new evidence in that order.
This document is not an investment recommendation; a judgment on price attractiveness and on position size reflecting a person's goals, horizon and loss tolerance is separate work.
paragraphs.qualification: The conditions are the author's analysis; the date of the confirmed results announcement was not found
